analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (a new shape-warmup section around head lines 956-989, plus unchanged surrounding text shown in the units) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1751, a new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP env var row). No executable code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization or storage logic changes in the supplied evidence.

Security relevance considered: the documented load-time shape warmup runs greedy probes and shape cells using the artifact's default sampling, with synthetic prompts, a 20-second wall budget, and no training of rates or counters. These would not use consumer data (A-001), so no exposure is evident. The env var `0` disables the warmup and `always` skips the shader-cache probe. This is a local operator-controlled knob, which is consistent with the existing operator-trust model (TB-003). It does not touch the prefix cache gating (T-041: DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, TTL, HMAC lookup), App Attest (TB-011), or the coordinator websocket (TB-002).

Remaining question for the next pass: the actual implementation (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift, shapeWarmup) is not supplied. I cannot verify that warmup prompts never touch the SSD prefix cache (donating synthetic prefixes) or run before the registration and authorization gates in a way that affects routing. The docs state the warmup runs before registration or before a standalone listener opens, and is excluded from rate training, so no regression is evident. The warmup may alter T-041 TTFT-oracle timing only marginally, since it affects cold-cache compile latency, not cache hit/miss behavior. No threat-model update is required from the docs alone.
